title: Restriction rules and scoping rules
objectives: Explain that a restriction rule further scopes already-shared read access to records matching criteria, permanently.
Explain that a scoping rule changes the default records a user sees without taking away sharing access.
Choose restriction versus scoping versus a tighter OWD or sharing design.
Refuse to treat scoping as a security substitute for restriction or FLS.
diagnostic_question: LAB_Support can open out-of-region Cases if they have the URL, but their list views are noisy. Compliance wants agents never to read another region's Cases. Restriction rule, scoping rule, or sharing redesign?
definition: A restriction rule further scopes the records a user could already read through sharing so only rows matching your criteria remain available; Help compares it to a list-view filter that is permanent. A scoping rule sets criteria so users see relevant records by default, but it does not restrict the record access they already have—they can still open and report on all records their sharing settings allow. ([Control Who Sees What](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_data_access.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for whether you use a restriction rule when the requirement is 'never read those rows' versus a scoping rule when the requirement is 'start on the relevant set.' Using scoping for compliance, or restriction for a UX filter, is a security miss.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a newsroom after you already have a building badge and desk keys (sharing). A restriction rule is an embargo lock on the wire: even with desk access, only matching stories come out, and the lock is permanent. A scoping rule is the default beat folder handed at shift start—they can still walk back and pull another allowed story if they know it is theirs to read.
deeper_explanation: Control Who Sees What: when a restriction rule is applied, data the user had read access to via sharing is further scoped to records matching the criteria. The behavior is similar to filtering a list view or report, except it is permanent. ([Control Who Sees What](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_data_access.htm))

Scoping rules set criteria to help users see relevant records. They do not restrict record access users already have. Users can still open and report on all records they can access per sharing settings. ([Control Who Sees What](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_data_access.htm))

Restriction rules are configured as metadata for supported objects and user criteria. Object availability, edition, and enablement are Needs verification in the target org. Do not invent a maximum number of rules. ([Restriction Rules](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_restriction_rule.htm))

Neither rule replaces object permissions or field-level security. A restriction rule cannot grant Read the user does not have. A scoping rule cannot hide a field. Sharing still cannot go below OWD; restriction is the documented way to narrow already-granted read access.

mental_model.analogy: A newsroom: restriction is an embargo lock on stories you could already reach; scoping is the default beat folder at shift start.

Apex, APIs, and reports may surface restriction differently; reverify current Restriction Rules Help for the access path you care about.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Restriction further scopes already-shared read access and is permanent. Scoping only changes the default set; users can still open and report on everything sharing allows. Neither is FLS or a way to go below OWD with a sharing rule.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the requirement verb. Never read: restriction if the object is supported, after sharing is already correct. Start focused: scoping. Should never have been shared: fix OWD or rules. Hide Amount: FLS. I will not invent rule limits. I test as the user with a matching and a non-matching LAB_ record, plus a URL or report test for scoping.

terminology.non_example: A sharing rule that grants more Cases.

terminology.non_example: A compliance lock that blocks URL access.

when_not_to_use: Do not use a scoping rule as a security lock; users can still open and report on shared records.
Do not use a restriction rule to hide a field; that is field-level security.
Do not use restriction to grant access the user does not have through sharing.
Do not invent restriction-rule counts or unsupported objects; verify Help in the org.

interview_questions.question: Contrast restriction rules and scoping rules.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Restriction permanently further scopes shared read access. Scoping only changes the default set; users can still open and report on shared records.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I quote Control Who Sees What. Restriction is the compliance lock after sharing. Scoping is a focus tool. I will not use scoping for never-read, and I will not use restriction to grant access. I verify object support instead of inventing limits. I test URL and report, not only list views.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Support_East cannot read LAB_Case_West under restriction; a lead with scoping still opens West.
follow_ups: What would you verify in the org?
Which later topic owns the rest?

interview_questions.question: Where do these rules sit relative to OWD and sharing rules?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: OWD and sharing decide the readable set first. Restriction can further scope that set. Sharing rules cannot go below OWD.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep SEC-004 in the answer. If peers should never have seen the rows, I fix the baseline. If the baseline is correct and a subset must disappear, I evaluate restriction. I do not call restriction a sharing rule. I do not call scoping a private OWD.
interview_questions.example: Public Read/Write plus scoping is not a privacy design for Cases.
follow_ups: What would you verify in the org?
Which later topic owns the rest?

interview_questions.question: Agents complain of noisy Case lists but must open transferred Cases from other regions.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: That is scoping, not restriction. Restriction would block the transfer read.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I ask whether a URL to the transferred Case must work. If yes, restriction is wrong. I still confirm object Read and sharing. I mark scoping enablement as Needs verification. I will not hide Subject with FLS to fake a region model.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Support_Lead keeps URL access to LAB_Case_West and gets an East-focused default list.
follow_ups: What would you verify in the org?
Which later topic owns the rest?

interview_questions.question: Security asks that support never read another region's Cases, including reports.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Restriction rule if Case is supported. Scoping is insufficient because reports and opens still work.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce a report as the agent. I confirm sharing first so I am not stacking restriction on a broken baseline. I test match and non-match. I document object support. I refuse a page-layout 'fix.'
interview_questions.example: LAB_Support_East report returns only East Cases after restriction.
follow_ups: What would you verify in the org?
Which later topic owns the rest?

interview_questions.question: When would you refuse both rules and redesign sharing?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the user should never have had a sharing path to those records. Fix OWD, roles, or rules first.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Restriction is not an apology for Public Read/Write without analysis. If the population is wrong at the baseline, I go back to SEC-004. If the need is a field, I use FLS. If the need is login, I leave this topic.
interview_questions.example: Peers seeing all Opportunities because OWD is Public: I do not start with scoping.
follow_ups: What would you verify in the org?
Which later topic owns the rest?

interview_questions.question: A restriction rule seems to do nothing.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I check user criteria, record criteria, object support, and whether I am testing as the intended user.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Admins often bypass what I am proving. I compare a matching and non-matching LAB_ record. I read Restriction Rules Help for the object. I check I did not build a scoping rule by mistake. I do not invent a cache timeout number.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Support_East still sees West because the user region field was blank.
follow_ups: What would you verify in the org?
Which later topic owns the rest?

interview_questions.question: How do you explain restriction to someone who only knows sharing rules?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Sharing rules add people to the readable set. Restriction subtracts rows from a set they already have, permanently.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw an arrow up for sharing and an arrow down for restriction. I remind them sharing cannot go below OWD, which is why restriction exists as a different feature. I give a region-Case example. I mention scoping so they do not misuse the word filter.
interview_questions.example: Owner-based sharing to a queue, then restriction by region for a subset of those users.
follow_ups: What would you verify in the org?
Which later topic owns the rest?

interview_questions.question: Teach restriction vs scoping with the newsroom-embargo analogy and break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Embargo lock on the wire is restriction; default beat folder is scoping. It breaks because not every object has the lock, and APIs may need a Help check.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk LAB_Support through the newsroom. I show a beat folder they can leave (scoping) and an embargo they cannot pick (restriction). I then say guest users, Apex keywords, and encryption are other buildings. I finish with: never call the beat folder a lock in a compliance meeting.
